summary: A connected Windows launch can reuse a session supplied in its process environment. configured_session checks the exact loopback origin before constructing an EditClient. Connected::load resolves the session and reads the protected board; the host remains responsible for authorization. Interactive sign-in and retries keep the client in memory.
evidence: windows_env_session_is_origin_scoped passed with fresh Windows processes. An absent configuration showed identifier entry. A different loopback port, either half of the pair alone, and a malformed token showed the sign-in form with a configuration warning. The selected test listener received zero connections across these launches.

With the correct origin, a valid session without a board grant showed No access to this board and no rows. After granting the same Member access, a fresh window showed ID 42 Review sketch above ID 17 Ink. A fresh PostgreSQL connection found exactly the original session verifier and account; independent board reads confirmed both rows at revision 1. Revoking that session returned the next launch to sign-in with the expiry message and zero sessions remained.

cargo test --locked -p boardcraft-desktop --features native-smoke --test windows_smoke -- --test-threads=1 passed all seven cases, including interactive rejection and correction and all five developer editor cases. Graphical retry after a transport outage was not separately exercised.

cargo test --locked --workspace passed all 18 portable tests. cargo fmt --all -- --check and git diff --check passed. The shell denied node --test scripts/run.test.mjs, so the Node runner regressions were not executed in this worker.
